newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBM says in Internet projects with Japan banks.
newsitem.headline: IBM says in Internet projects with Japan banks.

text.p: The chairman of International Business Machines Corp said on Friday that IBM and some Japanese banking clients have been engaged in "interesting" Internet-related projects, but declined to give details.
Louis Gerstner, speaking at his sixth annual news conference in Tokyo, said the company has "very interesting things going on with some Japanese banks related to Internet and on-line applications".

He declined to give details of the projects, but added: "Japanese banks have always been very sophisticated users of information technology, and I don't expect that to be anything less in the future."

To prepare for the Japanese government's "Big Bang" financial reform plan, Japanese banks are expected to boost investment to build efficient network computing systems to assist restructuring programmes.
Gerstner said IBM's strength in network computing was its ability to combine services, software, hardware and research to build solutions.
"On a global basis, delivering global solutions, I do not think there is anyone that has the assets that we have inside IBM," Gerstner said.

Referring to the liberalisation of the global telecommunications market following a World Trade Organisation agreement earlier this year, Gerstner said it would help bring down communications costs and benefit network computing firms.
